blocks.text: Action rules allow you to define the criteria for identifying specific data types and to automatically apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (formerly Microsoft Information Protection) sensitivity labels to files. For example, you can create an action rule to apply a Confidential label to a file that contains personally identifiable information (PII).

Currently, action rules only support the application of sensitivity labels to Azure file shares and on-premises SMB and NFS file shares based on specific criteria, such as DLP engines (e.g., PII, GDPR) and document types.
Action rules provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Gain visibility into files that are labeled and not labeled.
Secure sensitive data with consistent, content-based labeling.
Maintain data integrity and compliance by automatically tagging files containing sensitive data.

blocks.text: On the Action Rules page (Data Security > DSPM > Action Rules), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add an action rule.
DSPM scans and discovers the sensitivity labels every 12 hours. After you create an action rule, DSPM applies the labels every 4 hours.
View the list of action rules. For each action rule, you can see:
Rule Name: The name of the action rule.
Cloud: The cloud account type.
Scope: The scope defined for the action rule. Such as tenant (e.g., Zscaler DSPM Bravo), Azure File Share, and file types (e.g., CSV, DAT) to which the rule applies.
DLP Engines: The DLP Engines selected to classify sensitive data.
Document Types: The document types classified by the DLP Engine.
Action: The action (apply label) performed on the file that meets the rule criteria.
Rule Priority: The order in which the action rule is applied. The value can range from 1 to 2,000. A lower value (e.g., 1) indicates a higher priority.
Status: The state (Enabled, Disabled) of the action rule.
Last Updated: The date and time the action rule was last updated.
Sort the column data.
Search for a specific action rule.
Modify the table and its columns.
Enable or disable the action rule.
By default, the action rule is enabled.
Edit, delete, or update the priority of an action rule.
